name: fast.cu (H100 BF16 matmul kernels)
baseline: cuBLAS (cublasGemmEx, BF16 inputs, FP32 compute, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT); also CUB for the sum reduction
workload: Square BF16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation on an H100 (README gives N=4096 and N=8192); the repo also holds an H100 sum of 2^30 elements against CUB and a GB300 NVFP4 GEMM against a cuBLASLt baseline.
claimed_speedup: N=4096: kernel 763 TFLOPs vs cuBLAS 716 TFLOPs (about 1.07x, derived from page data); N=8192: 808 vs 795 TFLOPs (about 1.02x, derived from page data); sum of 2^30 elements: 3240.11 GB/s vs CUB 3193 GB/s (about 1.01x, derived from page data). The GB300 NVFP4 example lists no TFLOPs in the README.
compiler_and_flags: From the Makefile: nvcc -std=c++17 -O3 -DNDEBUG -w --expt-relaxed-constexpr --expt-extended-lambda --use_fast_math -Xcompiler=-fPIE -Xcompiler=-Wno-psabi -Xcompiler=-fno-strict-aliasing -gencode arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a, linked with -lcublas -lcuda. The CUDA toolkit version is not stated for the H100 kernels (the GB300 example asks for CUDA 13.1).
hardware: NVIDIA H100 (SXM or PCIe not stated); GB300/B300 for the NVFP4 example
tradeoffs: Hopper-only (sm_90a), BF16 with FP32 accumulate, square M=N=K problems in a fixed layout; the kernels are teaching/worklog snapshots (h100/matmul/ holds a ladder of kernels) and there is no general BLAS-style API, so it is a reference for kernel techniques rather than a drop-in cuBLAS replacement.
caveats: Margins over cuBLAS are small (1.02x to 1.07x). The harness in h100/matmul.cu hard-codes max_size = 8192 and times 8 repeats with CUDA events, so the README's N=4096 number needs an edit to reproduce. It calls cublasGemmEx with CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT, not an autotuned cuBLASLt algorithm, and verifies each kernel against that cuBLAS output. No GPU clock lock, driver or CUDA version is recorded. The linked worklog (cudaforfun.substack.com) was not opened because substack is blocked here. Borderline A: code, flags (Makefile) and GPU model are public; only the CUDA version and H100 variant are missing. Baseline is cuBLAS, not one of OpenBLAS/MKL/Eigen/BLIS.
found_via: WebSearch without a domain filter, query 'FP32 matmul faster than cuBLAS 4090 H100 github Show HN' (a follow-up to the Hacker News hit 'Show HN: FP32 matmul of large matrices up to 24% faster than cuBLAS on a 4090'). Whether the worklog was itself submitted to Hacker News was not confirmed because news.ycombinator.com cannot be opened here. Opened the repo page, the commits page, and README.md, Makefile and h100/matmul.cu via raw.githubusercontent.com.

name: Faster_SGEMM_CUDA (arekpaterek)
workload: FP32 matmul of large square matrices on an RTX 4090 (title of the Show HN thread); search-result summaries of the thread also mention other GPUs (snippet only, unverified).
claimed_speedup: Snippet only. Hacker News thread title (item 41122018, as returned by search): 'FP32 matmul of large matrices up to 24% faster than cuBLAS on a 4090'. Search-result summaries of the thread, not verified against any page I could open: 24% on 12288^2 and 16384^2 on the 4090; +13% to +21% on a 4070 TS; +56% to +76% on a T4; +9% to +23% on an H100 (4096^2 to 12288^2); up to +43% at 12288^2 on an A100.
hardware: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (from the thread title); other GPUs only from snippets
tradeoffs: Unknown: the code could not be read. The repo name suggests a CUDA SGEMM kernel derived from the well-known SGEMM_CUDA worklog series, but this is inferred from the name only.
caveats: Repo is unreachable: https://github.com/arekpaterek/Faster_SGEMM_CUDA returned 404 on WebFetch and on raw.githubusercontent.com (README.md on HEAD, main and master), the owner's public repository list shows only two unrelated 2048 forks, and the forks list of siboehm/SGEMM_CUDA has no matching fork. A search-result summary also noted that the repo had been reported as 404 at times. Every number comes from search-result summaries of the Hacker News thread, which I could not open (egress blocked); the title is the only exact quote. No compiler, flags, CUDA version, license or code could be checked, so has_code is false and the claim is capped at tier C. The language is inferred from the repo name. Baseline is cuBLAS, not one of OpenBLAS/MKL/Eigen/BLIS. Kept as a flagged lead so a verifier can look for a mirror or the thread's own benchmark post.
found_via: Hacker News via WebSearch with allowed_domains news.ycombinator.com: query 'Show HN faster matrix multiplication than OpenBLAS MKL' returned the thread 'Show HN: FP32 matmul of large matrices up to 24% faster than cuBLAS on a 4090' (item 41122018); a second Hacker News query naming that title returned the repo URL.
